note: Triage rules written from general knowledge. The FCA Handbook was INACCESSIBLE in this environment (sources/audits/fca.md); every sourcebook reference must be checked against the point-in-time Handbook before reliance. Not legal advice.

verification_values.partially_corroborated_secondary: supported by secondary snippets recorded in the audit; primary text not read

rules.title: Perimeter guidance - is the activity regulated and which permission applies
rules.why: Every UK credit/mortgage-related service must first establish whether its activities (e.g. arranging, advising, lending, credit broking, operating an information/comparison service) are regulated activities and need permission.
rules.provenance: FCA Handbook PERG (perimeter guidance manual); specific chapters for mortgages and consumer credit not checked - Handbook INACCESSIBLE in this environment

rules.title: Criteria-search / information service: arranging or advising boundary
rules.why: A tool that matches customers to lenders' criteria may cross from information into arranging or advising depending on how results are presented and whether introductions are made; boundary needs a reasoned legal view.
rules.provenance: General knowledge of the arranging/advising boundary under the Regulated Activities Order and PERG; article numbers deliberately not cited (unverified)

rules.title: Authorisation status and scope of Part 4A permission or appointed-representative arrangement
rules.why: The firm arranges, advises or lends, so its permissions (or principal firm's cover) must match each activity and product.
rules.provenance: FSMA Part 4A permissions and Threshold Conditions (COND) - from general knowledge (unverified)

rules.title: Mortgages and Home Finance: Conduct of Business sourcebook applies to regulated mortgage activity
rules.why: Consumer first- or second-charge mortgage products are in scope of MCOB conduct rules for firms carrying on regulated mortgage activities.
rules.provenance: FCA Handbook MCOB; second-charge mortgages brought under FCA mortgage rules from 21 March 2016 (secondary corroboration - FCA factsheet snippet, see sources/audits/fca.md)

rules.title: Responsible lending and affordability assessment
rules.why: Lenders must assess affordability before entering into or varying a regulated mortgage contract; a platform that computes affordability indicators must not misrepresent them as the lender's assessment.
rules.provenance: FCA Handbook MCOB 11.6 (responsible lending) - partially corroborated by secondary snippets; possible carve-outs for some second-charge cases unresolved

rules.title: Advised vs non-advised (execution-only) sales standards
rules.why: How the service interacts with the customer determines which selling standards apply (advice, execution-only, or neither).
rules.provenance: FCA Handbook MCOB chapter on advising and selling standards - chapter number not verified

rules.title: Second-charge mortgage considerations incl. legacy/transitional provisions
rules.why: Second-charge mortgages moved from consumer credit to mortgage regulation in 2016; some legacy contracts have transitional treatment and some MCOB provisions differ for second charges.
rules.provenance: FCA factsheet on second charge mortgages (secondary snippet) and MCOB 12 transitional snippets; not read in primary form

rules.title: Financial promotions for mortgage products
rules.why: Marketing or displaying mortgage products to consumers is a financial promotion and must be fair, clear and not misleading and, where required, signed off by an authorised person (s21 approval regime - unverified).
rules.provenance: FCA Handbook MCOB financial promotion chapter and FSMA s21 - from general knowledge (unverified)

rules.title: Consumer Credit sourcebook for non-mortgage consumer credit and credit broking
rules.why: Unsecured consumer credit lending or broking is within CONC (creditworthiness, pre-contract information, broking conduct).
rules.provenance: FCA Handbook CONC - scope NOT corroborated in this session (see sources/audits/fca.md)

rules.title: Deferred payment credit (BNPL) regulatory status
rules.why: The regulatory status of interest-free deferred payment credit has been subject to legislative change in the UK; current status and commencement dates must be checked before any conclusion.
rules.provenance: General knowledge of UK BNPL regulation plans; dates and scope deliberately not stated (unverified)

rules.title: Consumer Duty outcomes for retail customers
rules.why: Firms whose activities affect outcomes for retail customers must deliver good outcomes (products and services, price and value, consumer understanding, consumer support) and avoid foreseeable harm.
rules.provenance: FCA Handbook PRIN 2A; in force 31 July 2023 for open products and 31 July 2024 for closed products (secondary corroboration, see sources/audits/fca.md)

rules.title: Customers in vulnerable circumstances
rules.why: Vulnerable customers are expected in this market; design, communications and support must account for them and outcomes should be monitored.
rules.provenance: FCA guidance on fair treatment of vulnerable customers (reference number not verified) and PRIN 2A

rules.title: Systems and controls, governance, record keeping and outsourcing
rules.why: Authorised firms need governance, risk management, record keeping and oversight of outsourced/critical services (including technology suppliers).
rules.provenance: FCA Handbook SYSC - from general knowledge (unverified)

rules.title: Governance of AI/automated decision components
rules.why: Use of AI in eligibility, affordability or recommendations needs model governance, explainability to staff and customers, testing for bias and clear accountability under existing FCA rules.
rules.provenance: Existing FCA requirements (SYSC, Consumer Duty) applied to AI - general knowledge; no AI-specific FCA rule asserted (unverified)

rules.title: Complaints handling and Financial Ombudsman Service
rules.why: Firms dealing with eligible complainants need complaint-handling procedures, time limits, FOS referral rights and reporting.
rules.provenance: FCA Handbook DISP - scope NOT corroborated in this session (see sources/audits/fca.md)

rules.title: Business customers: check whether any customers fall within consumer protections
rules.why: Lending to businesses is often unregulated, but some small businesses (e.g. sole traders, small partnerships) and some secured lending can fall within consumer credit or mortgage regulation; confirm per product.
rules.provenance: General knowledge; thresholds deliberately not stated (unverified)

rules.title: Personal data processing, lawful basis, DPIA
rules.why: Customer financial data is personal data; lawful basis, transparency, minimisation, retention and a DPIA for high-risk processing must be considered.
rules.provenance: UK GDPR / DPA 2018 - outside the FCA Handbook and outside this library's source registry (unverified)
rules.signoff_role: Legal counsel and Data Protection Officer

rules.title: Solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects
rules.why: Automated eligibility or affordability outputs may engage restrictions on solely automated decision-making and require human review routes and explanations.
rules.provenance: UK GDPR Article 22-type provisions and ICO guidance - outside the source registry; article number and recent amendments not verified
rules.signoff_role: Legal counsel and Data Protection Officer

rules.title: Indirect discrimination in criteria, models and journeys
rules.why: Criteria (age, employment type, income source) and models can disadvantage people with protected characteristics; justification and reasonable adjustments must be assessed.
rules.provenance: Equality Act 2010 - outside the FCA Handbook and outside the source registry (unverified)
